- Note 3 (ticket 2): role Payroll Specialist, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read, comment explains Security DB confirms contractor with basic training, max is read, requested write exceeds max, recommend read.

Wait, there's conflicting info: Note 1 says full_time, Note 2/3 say contractor. The most recent notes (ticket 2) say contractor with basic security training. The HR and Security agents' notes conflict on employment type? Note 1 says full_time (maybe HR), Note 2 says contractor (maybe security). Note 3 confirms contractor with basic training and recommends read.

The policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

If contractor with basic security training, max = read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant max = read.

Note 1 says full_time - if full_time, max for Source Code would be write (Payroll Specialist doesn't own Source Code, Engineer does), so could grant write. But notes 2 and 3 say contractor, with latest note confirming contractor. The Security DB confirms contractor. The recommendation is read.

Given conflicting employment types, the most recent and corroborated info (notes 2 & 3) say contractor with basic training. So max is read. Requested write > read, so grant read.

I'll submit decision: read.
